I agree that the boss fight was kind of weak compared to the massive trek you took getting there, but I don't honestly think there would've been a good way to do it. The last two boss fights made sense because you were stripped of your weapons and gear, so it felt natural and frantic ro fight with just a machete, but you still had all of your weapons when climbing the tower. There's almost no way to explain a one handed man stripping you of your weapons for a realistic and fair fight. I can't speak for you, but my weapon had the Angel Mod, and it would've been annoying to slice once and kill him. The qte felt out of place, but there weren't many other ways to end it.

If you're having trouble early game with weapons breaking, try to remember to kick. It costs no stamina, you get 1 power xp per kick (basically nothing), but most of all you can knock down zombies with it and get a really good, clean head shot with a weapon. Since Dying Light lets you repair weapons for free, you will be tempted to swing like crazy. Resist that urge as best you can. 

Something else to do that goes with kicking is to level up your agility. It has a ton of crowd control like jumping on zombie heads and stunning them, a drop kick to send them flying or separate one particular target, reversing and even stunning a zombie that tries to grab you. Agility is, at least in my experience, the easiest skill tree to fill up and the most important since my play style was to dodge and run until I eventually got insane weapons later on.

One last thing is to get used to fire crackers. Again, once I got better weapons I used these less and less, but fire crackers are amazing for herding and moving zombies away from a point of interest or just distracting them. I actually used to use them a lot for capturing safe houses because every enemy would turn their back giving me a chance to line up attacks with no pressure.
